summary: A large, asymmetrical building complex featuring a main hall with a steep, stepped brick roof and a prominent, semi-detached square tower. The walls are constructed from a yellowish brick-like block, heavily accented with white horizontal bands and vertical pillars. The tower features a flat, overhanging roof.

shape.overall_form: asymmetrical complex consisting of a main hall and a tall square tower

materials.name: brick
materials.role: main roof and tower roof trim

materials.name: quartz_block
materials.role: horizontal banding, vertical pillars, and low perimeter wall

materials.name: slab_stone
materials.role: main roof ridge cap and flat tower roof

rebuild_hints: Construct the main roof using brick blocks in a steep, stepped formation rather than standard stairs, capping the very top ridge with smooth stone slabs.
Build the walls using a yellowish block (like end stone bricks or sandstone), adding prominent horizontal bands of white blocks to separate the first and second floors.
The tower should be built as a separate vertical structure, capped with a flat roof made of smooth stone slabs with a red brick trim underneath the overhang.
Surround the base of the structure with a low, single-block high wall of white blocks.
Insert small, mostly 1x1 or 1x2 glass pane windows regularly along the walls between the white banding.
uncertainties: The exact block types for the yellow walls (end stone bricks vs. sandstone) and white accents (quartz vs. white concrete/wool) are uncertain due to distance.
The rear facade, interior layout, and exact depth of the building are completely hidden from view.
The exact footprint and structural connection point between the tower and the main building are obscured by the angle.
